idiom_name: typedef for the strategy signature plus a function pointer in the context struct
implementation_notes: C has no classes, no virtual dispatch and no closures, so the strategy interface becomes a typedef for the function signature and the concrete strategy is an ordinary function; the context is a struct whose field of that function-pointer type is the strategy slot. This is exactly the shape the standard library uses: qsort and bsearch take the ordering strategy as a comparison function pointer, and glibc's qsort_r shows the workaround for the missing closure - the comparator receives an extra void * argument through which it reaches its configuration, keeping the call reentrant and thread-safe. Use the ops-table variant instead as soon as the strategy has more than one operation or must be selected at run time by name.
pitfalls: A function pointer carries no state: configuration must travel through an explicit void * argument (the qsort_r pattern) or a file-scope variable - the latter makes the strategy non-reentrant and unsafe under threads.

The typedef must match the concrete functions exactly; a mismatched signature is at best a warning and the call is undefined behaviour, so never launder a strategy through an incompatible pointer type.
A function pointer can legally be NULL, so a context initialised without a strategy crashes on the first call; constructors must validate the slot or install a defined no-op/default strategy.

variants.name: Static const table of function pointers (hand-written vtable)
variants.idiom_name: struct of function pointers, one static const instance per algorithm
variants.implementation_notes: When the strategy bundles several related operations (encode/decode, open/read/close), group the function pointers into a struct and keep one static const instance per algorithm - the same shape a C++ vtable has - while the context holds only a pointer to the table plus an opaque state pointer. Selection then happens once (by configuration or by name in a registry) and every call is a single table lookup, which is how C libraries expose driver and codec families. The table must be complete and its layout stable; C99 designated initialisers at least make a reordering of the struct survivable.
pitfalls: A missing initialiser leaves a NULL slot that only fails when that operation is called; every table needs a constructor-time completeness check (or a test that exercises each slot).
The table is shared, so the state pointer must be per context: storing mutable state in the table (or in file-scope variables beside it) makes every user of that algorithm share it.
Nothing in the type system ties a table to the state layout it expects; each ops table must document the state struct it casts its void *state to, or the two families drift apart silently.
